commits.message:
Markdown hands a quote's content a cell count, never a negative width (rich-unfiled-791c.hlmh)

Review fixes: the quote's narrowed width goes through cellCount, so a quote at width 0 or 1 no longer passes guttered a negative maxWidth. The quote table's test titles name their options, so the two justify rows are told apart, and the older bar test it duplicated is gone. The one-cell floor in guttered that departs from Rich at narrow widths is rich-unfiled-791c.jra3.

Markdown lays a quote's content out four cells short of the width, as Rich's BlockQuote does (rich-unfiled-791c.hlmh)

A quote's text now wraps, rules and justifies at the width less four beside its two-cell bar, so its rows end two cells short, byte for byte with Rich 15's output for wrapped text, a rule, justify and a nested quote.

Markdown ends a list at the second blank line after an empty item, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.tx0u) (#447)

* Markdown ends a list at the second blank line after an empty item, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.tx0u)

markdown-it's list rule, for an item whose content is empty and whose next
line is blank, skips to the line two past it without tokenizing and checks
that line for the next item, skipping no more blank lines. '-\n\n\n- a' is
two lists there; it was one here. Pinned against Rich 15 (markdown-it-py 4.2).

* Markdown measures the step past an empty item from where the item ends (rich-unfiled-791c.tx0u)

Review: both branches now count from `end`, one blank line skipped after an
empty item and all of them after any other. Container cases are pinned with
ordered items, where one list and two number differently; bullets draw the
same either way in Rich.

* Markdown takes markdown-it's empty-item step only when the marker line has no content (rich-unfiled-791c.tx0u)

The previous commit decided it from the line where the item ends, so an item
whose content starts on its second line ('1.\n   foo\n\n\n1. b') stepped over
one blank line and split the list. It is markdown-it's condition again: the
line after the marker is blank, and the step lands two lines on.
